userStories.title: Parse unified-diff new-side line ranges
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a pure unified-diff parser that returns each changed file’s eligible new-side line ranges.

**Motivation** — A survivor on an untouched line is not evidence about *this story’s* tests; it is a pre-existing coverage gap attributed to an unrelated change.

**Approach** — Filter **at generation**: `generateMutants` receives the eligible line ranges and skips lines outside them, using the same `continue` that already skips comment lines. Ranges come from **one** `git diff --unified=0 <ref>` per story, parsed into a map, not a spawn per file. Add `extractDiffLineRanges` beside the existing `extractDiffFiles` in `src/utils/diff-files.ts`, sharing its header conventions. Pure function, no I/O.

**Scope** — In: parsing `+++ b/` file headers and `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` new-side hunks, including CRLF, omissions, deletions, and malformed input tolerance. Out: git invocation, absolute path anchoring, mutant generation, operation wiring, and summary rendering.

**Interface**
```typescript
export interface LineRange { readonly start: number; readonly end: number }  // 1-based, inclusive, new side
export function extractDiffLineRanges(diff: string): Map<string, LineRange[]>
```

**Design notes** — For a header `@@ -a,b +c,d @@`, the range is `{start: c, end: c + d - 1}`. Omitted counts mean 1; a new-side count of 0 yields no range. `+++ /dev/null` produces no map entry. Binary files produce no hunks and yield no entry. Renames report the new path on the `+++` side and need no special handling. Parser never throws; unrecognised lines are ignored and whatever parsed cleanly is returned.
acceptanceCriteria: When `extractDiffLineRanges` is called with a diff string, then it returns a `Map`.
Given `+++ b/src/a.ts` and hunk `@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@`, when `extractDiffLineRanges` parses the diff, then `map.get("src/a.ts")` equals `[{ start: 1, end: 5 }]`.
Given hunk `@@ -1 +1 @@`, when `extractDiffLineRanges` parses the diff, then its produced range equals `{ start: 1, end: 1 }`.
Given hunk `@@ -5,3 +0,0 @@`, when `extractDiffLineRanges` parses the diff, then it produces no range for that file.
Given a diff containing hunks for two files, when `extractDiffLineRanges` parses it, then the map has one entry per file and each entry contains only that file’s ranges.
Given a file header `+++ /dev/null`, when `extractDiffLineRanges` parses the diff, then the map has no entry for that file.

Given one file with hunks `@@ -10,0 +11,2 @@` and `@@ -30,0 +40,1 @@`, when `extractDiffLineRanges` parses the diff, then its entry equals `[{ start: 11, end: 12 }, { start: 40, end: 40 }]` in that order.
Given equivalent CRLF and LF diffs, when `extractDiffLineRanges` parses each, then the returned maps are equal.
When `extractDiffLineRanges("")` is called, then it returns an empty `Map`.
Given a diff containing recognised headers and unrecognised lines, when `extractDiffLineRanges` parses it, then it returns ranges from the recognised headers without throwing.

routing.reasoning: A single existing pure utility and its established unit-test suite gain a focused parser with no I/O or cross-module integration.

userStories.title: Fetch and anchor changed line ranges
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a fail-open fetcher that obtains one unified-zero diff and returns its parsed ranges keyed by absolute path.

**Motivation** — The mutation spot-check mutates whole changed **files** rather than the lines a story changed, so a surviving mutant may sit on code the story never touched.

**Approach** — New module wrapping one `git diff --unified=0` call and anchoring parsed paths to absolute form. `getChangedNonTestFiles` (`src/verification/smart-runner.ts:399`) is the model for the new fetcher: `gitWithTimeout` for the spawn, `baseRef ?? "HEAD~1"` for the default ref, and a `try/catch` returning a neutral value rather than throwing.

**Scope** — In: the fetcher, injectable git collaborators, parsing integration, default-ref behavior, and git-root/workdir absolute anchoring. Out: package filtering and pathspec scoping, which remain owned by `getChangedNonTestFiles`; mutant generation and operation integration belong to US-003.

**Interface**
```typescript
export async function getChangedLineRanges(
  workdir: string,
  baseRef?: string,
): Promise<Map<string, LineRange[]> | null>
```

**Design notes** — Keys in the returned map are **absolute paths**. `getChangedNonTestFiles` already performs prefix surgery for the case where the git root sits above `repoRoot`, and the op anchors its results into `absoluteChangedFiles`; keying absolutely lets the op look up by a value it already holds instead of duplicating that logic where it can drift. The parser works at the git level and knows nothing about languages. No `process.cwd()` — `workdir` stays threaded as a parameter. A non-zero diff exit or thrown spawn returns `null`; successful empty output returns an empty map.
acceptanceCriteria: When `getChangedLineRanges` receives a successful git response, then it resolves to a `Map`.
Given a supplied base ref, when `getChangedLineRanges` calls its injected git runner, then the arguments are `["diff", "--unified=0", baseRef]` in that order.
When `getChangedLineRanges` is called without `baseRef`, then its injected git runner receives `HEAD~1` as the ref.
Given an injected git response with a non-zero exit code, when `getChangedLineRanges` runs, then it resolves to `null`.
Given an injected git runner that throws, when `getChangedLineRanges` runs, then it resolves to `null` without propagating the error.
Given a successful injected git response with empty stdout, when `getChangedLineRanges` runs, then it resolves to an empty `Map` rather than `null`.
Given git root `/repo` and a diff path `src/a.ts`, when `getChangedLineRanges` runs, then the returned map key is `/repo/src/a.ts`.
Given a git-root lookup resolving to `null`, when `getChangedLineRanges` anchors a parsed path, then the key is rooted at the supplied `workdir`.
Given git output with hunk `@@ -0,0 +2,3 @@` for one file, when `getChangedLineRanges` runs, then that file’s absolute-keyed entry contains `{ start: 2, end: 4 }`.

routing.reasoning: This adds a small I/O wrapper with injected git behavior, path anchoring, and explicit fail-open handling across three established utility seams.

userStories.title: Scope mutation candidates to changed lines
acceptanceCriteria: Given `lineRanges` covering only line 5, when `generateMutants` runs, then every returned mutant has `line === 5`.
Given a mutable line equal to a range start, when `generateMutants` runs with that range, then it includes a mutant for that line.
Given a mutable line equal to a range end, when `generateMutants` runs with that range, then it includes a mutant for that line.
Given two disjoint `lineRanges`, when `generateMutants` runs, then it returns mutants from both ranges and none from lines between them.
When `generateMutants` is called without `lineRanges`, then it returns mutants for every mutable source line as before.
When `generateMutants` is called with an empty `lineRanges` array, then it returns no mutants.
Given injected `getChangedLineRanges` resolves to `null`, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` runs, then it returns `success: true` with outcomes `{ killed: 0, survived: 0, errored: 0 }`.
Given injected `getChangedLineRanges` resolves to `null`, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` runs, then it never invokes injected `regression`.
Given injected `getChangedLineRanges` resolves to `null`, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` runs, then it emits a warning containing the story id.
Given a changed file absent from the returned range map, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` runs, then it generates no mutants for that file and resolves with `success: true`.
Given a changed file absent from the returned range map, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` runs, then it emits a debug log containing the story id and file path.
Given a changed file whose map entry has ranges, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` generates candidates for it, then `generateMutants` receives those same `lineRanges`.
When `mutationCheckOp.execute` runs, then it invokes injected `getChangedLineRanges` exactly once with the story `workdir` and `storyGitRef`.
Given a file whose ranges contain no mutable content, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` runs, then it resolves with `success: true` and never invokes injected `regression`.
Given a file whose ranges contain no mutable content, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` runs, then it emits no warning for that file.

routing.reasoning: This changes the candidate-generation contract and composes a new git-derived dependency through the advisory operation while preserving package scoping, error behavior, and many existing test fixtures.

outOfScope: `operators.ts` has no direct test file; adding `test/unit/verification/mutation/operators.test.ts` and covering the untested operator ids is deferred (gap item G6).
`selectScopedTests` is recomputed per mutant although it is loop-invariant; hoisting it is deferred (gap item G8).
Mutant dedupe across operators and equivalent-mutant detection are deferred (gap item G13).
Content-verified revert (revert is positional today) is deferred (gap item G9).
Crash and interrupt cleanup for a partially applied mutant is deferred (gap item G10).
No config key is added to choose between diff-scoped and whole-file candidate generation; diff-scoped is the only behaviour.
Deleted lines are not mutated; only added and modified lines on the new side of the diff are eligible.

userStories.title: Surface candidate counts and unchecked stories
acceptanceCriteria: Given mutation checking is enabled and candidates are generated, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` records the story summary, then `checked === true`.
Given `mutationCheck.enabled === false`, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` records the story summary, then `checked === false`.
Given no resolvable test command, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` records the story summary, then `checked === false`.
Given injected `getChangedLineRanges` resolves to `null`, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` records the story summary, then `checked === true` and `candidates === 0`.
Given generated mutation candidates, when `mutationCheckOp.execute` records the story summary, then `candidates` equals the number generated before budget selection.
Given one summary with `checked: true` and `candidates: 0`, when `formatMutationSummary` runs, then its text contains `NOT CHECKED` and that summary’s story id.
Given one summary with `checked: false` and `candidates: 0`, when `formatMutationSummary` runs, then its text omits `NOT CHECKED`.
Given one summary with `checked: true` and `candidates > 0`, when `formatMutationSummary` runs, then its text omits `NOT CHECKED`.

Given one summary with a survivor and another with `checked: true` and `candidates: 0`, when `formatMutationSummary` runs, then its text contains both `SURVIVING MUTANTS` and `NOT CHECKED` with `SURVIVING MUTANTS` first.
Given two summaries with `checked: true` and `candidates: 0`, when `formatMutationSummary` runs, then the `NOT CHECKED` block lists both story ids.
Given only summaries with `checked: false`, when `formatMutationSummary` runs, then it returns an empty string.

routing.reasoning: This is a focused cross-module additive summary-contract change with clear early-return semantics and formatter behavior.

analysis: This is an enhancement to the existing advisory mutation spot-check, not a greenfield subsystem. `src/utils/diff-files.ts:14` currently provides a pure `extractDiffFiles` parser using `+++ b/` headers, so the line-range parser belongs beside it and must retain CRLF and `/dev/null` behavior. `src/verification/smart-runner.ts:399` supplies the fail-open `getChangedNonTestFiles` model: default `HEAD~1`, `gitWithTimeout`, package filtering, git-root prefix surgery, and a neutral catch result. `src/utils/git.ts:37` exposes `getGitRoot`, while `gitWithTimeout` at line 54 is the required shared process wrapper. `src/verification/mutation/mutator.ts:14` currently generates candidates from every non-comment source line; adding an optional range filter there preserves the generator as the single, pure eligibility point and keeps source-coordinate reporting unchanged. `src/operations/mutation-check.ts:55` exposes the established `MutationCheckDeps` DI seam and at lines 110-135 converts scoped relative changed files to absolute paths then calls `generateMutants`; it must fetch a single absolute-keyed range map once per story, skip absent entries, and count all pre-budget candidates. This is the primary integration and compatibility risk: every complete fake dependency object in `test/unit/operations/mutation-check.test.ts:28` and `test/unit/operations/mutation-check-selection.test.ts:42` must gain a range fetcher, and existing changed-file fixtures need matching ranges or they intentionally produce no candidates. `src/runtime/mutation-summary.ts:9` has a closed summary shape consumed by `src/log-format/mutation-summary.ts:3`, which currently only renders survivors; both types and existing exact-shape test fixtures need additive `candidates` and `checked` fields. The operation remains fail-open: diff read failures, malformed diffs, files absent from the range map, non-mutable ranges, and file reads never block the story. No migration or configuration change is needed: diff scoping becomes the only behavior, package scoping stays in `getChangedNonTestFiles`, and public internal callers of `generateMutants` remain compatible because `lineRanges` is optional. Relevant tests already exist in `test/unit/utils/diff-files.test.ts:4`, `test/unit/verification/mutation/mutator.test.ts:11`, `test/unit/operations/mutation-check.test.ts:28`, `test/unit/operations/mutation-check-selection.test.ts:42`, and `test/unit/log-format/mutation-summary.test.ts:5`; the new operation-level diff-scope suite must be split out because the existing main operation suite is near its 800-line hard limit.
outOfScope: `operators.ts` has no direct test file; adding `test/unit/verification/mutation/operators.test.ts` and covering the untested operator ids is deferred (gap item G6).
`selectScopedTests` is recomputed per mutant although it is loop-invariant; hoisting it is deferred (gap item G8).
Mutant dedupe across operators and equivalent-mutant detection are deferred (gap item G13).
Serial mutant execution, the flat per-mutant timeout, and the absence of a run-level time budget are unchanged (gap item G14).
Content-verified revert (revert is positional today) is deferred (gap item G9).
Crash and interrupt cleanup for a partially applied mutant is deferred (gap item G10).
No config key is added to choose between diff-scoped and whole-file candidate generation; diff-scoped is the only behaviour.
Mutants are not tagged with in-diff or out-of-diff provenance, and the surviving-mutant report does not distinguish them.
The `execution.mutationCheck.maxMutants` default stays at 3; retuning it against field evidence is deferred.
Deleted lines are not mutated; only added and modified lines on the new side of the diff are eligible.
